metadata.title: The Nuclear Cluster of the Milky Way: Total Mass and Luminosity (long version)

notes: No eligible stars. The paper's "unbound" stars are unbound from the SMBH/nuclear cluster, not the Milky Way: S111/ID 770 has only a minimum binding mass above the SMBH (T:p18-b15); the nine stars unbound for some assumed distances, including S111 and ID 569, are used for an R0 estimate (T:p18-b17); and the fast stars at R > 10'' are described as "not bound to the GC," with a preferred interpretation as stars on very eccentric orbits in the larger-scale potential rather than Galactic escapees (T:p19-b7, T:p20-b1). Table 5's fast stars (IDs 770/S111, 569, 4/IRS 9, 4258, 899, 903, 787) are not explicitly identified as Galactic unbound candidates (T:p21-b0). ID 787 is only described as a prior "runaway candidate" from Schödel et al. (2009), a label that does not establish Galactic-unbound candidacy, and the present paper weakens that status (T:p20-b10).
